Video_Title: Something Very Bad is Going to Happen (2026) Netflix Review
Comment:
I love horror thrillers and dark psychological themes, so I was genuinely excited for Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen. Unfortunately, this series is about four episodes too long. What could have been a tense, atmospheric slow-burn ends up feeling aggressively stretched out to fill time. By the halfway point, the pacing becomes so dragged out that it actually starts destroying the suspense and dread the show worked so hard to create in the beginning.

The biggest problem is how manipulative the storytelling feels. The series constantly hints at shocking revelations and sinister meanings without giving enough payoff to justify the endless lingering scenes and cryptic behavior. Early on, the family is presented as deeply unsettling and almost frightening, but later episodes suddenly portray them as fairly normal and functional people, making a lot of the earlier tension feel artificial rather than meaningful.

And what happened to the dogs? The show introduces details like they’re important pieces of the mystery, then either forgets them completely or expects the audience not to notice. That kind of inconsistency keeps happening throughout the series.

There are good ideas here, and the atmosphere in the first few episodes is genuinely effective, but the show becomes so bloated and repetitive that it loses its impact. Instead of building tension, it stalls it. What should have been a sharp, disturbing four-episode thriller gets diluted into an overextended series that mistakes slow pacing for depth.

Verizon offers $10 for Netflix + HBO/Max … and $10 for Hulu, Disney, ESPN. 

During holidays it is easy to get a discounted app. Like Hulu last Christmas was $24 for the year. Same with MAX for $3 for six months. This is true for a lot of services. 

I think using a service for a blocked amount of time then dropping it. And signing up for another discounted option. Etc. Rotate services to enjoy and binge.

Like in summer people are outside a lot so drop services. Then toward fall when discounts start popping up try one.

Another thing, the cbs app and others like NBC allow shows the week of airing or the following week for free. For a period of time. Then lock them for paid members.

This is OG. Meaning schedule television when it is actually aired. I write shows I like down on a calendar or might set a reminder on my phone.

The idea of tv on demand is a device to get people to spend more. Who cares about commercials. At least we have the mute button. Unlike back in the day.

But when advertisers made commercials louder because people would leave the room to use the bathroom so we could hear them it was really just a timer so we would know when the show starts again. To get back into the room.

Another tip, for free channels like Tubi and Pluto there’s a save either plus sign or looks like a ribbon cut out to tap. This saves the video under “my stuff”. 

Many people have prime so lots of movie options.

For YouTube, the free movies, how to save, tap the movie on, while it starts to play. Scroll to the ribbon save tab. And create a file on the phone on the YouTube app under your account when tapping the tab to create a playlist. Name it movies. Or for music similar. Then tap save. And it’ll be there until YT removes that movie for another since movies usually rotate to different services.

Another hack for prime folk. If you use the order service, and don’t mind receiving an item the following week Amazon may offer digital dollars. 

Take these. They add up. Wait for sales on favorite movies. Like during holidays there might be a sale on a favorite movie. 

You can buy it for no cost using digital dollars.

I understand that times change but just because things change doesn't always mean it was for the better. 

I'd argue that the methods today because they don't do longer contracts up front, they didn't build long-term sets, they don't use the same company often for much of their CGI and so forth. I know you cannot do things exactly the same but much of those could be retooled for today. The CGI company changes because they go for the lowest bidder and have no unions. Not because the method is better.

Not quite sure if a very cheap Olympic barbell can't be worth it. I've seen 450 lbs rated Olympic barbells for less than $150 or even as low as $100 on sale. For a lot of people that's a perfect investment. And whenever you want a better barbell, the old one can still fill a different purpose.

If you have a strict budget and it's either a better barbell or a rack without spotter arms, always go with the cheaper barbell. During the madness back in 2020 I bought a $35 barbell for 25 mm weights. I loaded up 350 lbs on one side of it for some "living room-friendly" belt squats and deadlifts from car jack stands. Shabby, but it did the job. Granted, I of course didn't throw it around or abuse it, but it was $35! Weeeeeell worth the investment. Comment: I own this lat pulldown and it is phenominal, wish he would've fixed the cables to demo it better. Some notes on it for future buyers: It's short. It fits under 7 foot ceilings so perfectly in my basement. That's why I got it. I dont have the headroom for a taller machine. Also because of the price it was a good deal. I want to mention 2 things: 1. I'm 5'11 and I am BARELY able to get a full stretch, but you can even take the pin out of the seat and the seat goes down another inch or so and that gives me a stretch perfectly where I dont hit the top. If you're 6'1 or smaller it should work for you. Secondly, you'll notice the seat is in the way for something like bicep curls BUT if you do the hack I mentioned before then the seat is just resting in the hole so you can just remove it completely in a second and now nothing gets in the way of doing vertical pulling movements from the low row cable. Really clever hack there! Also, I greased the back upright and now it slides really well. Not perfect but I wouldnt change anything about it. Honestly, the only cons are that its not bolted down and doesnt have a way to weigh it down so doing standing face pulls for example will make the machine tip (I havent tipped it yet). Otherwise recommend! And also its amazon so if you're too tall for it, you can return it. But again that was a big fear of mine but its literally just tall enough to work. I think it will fit most people.

Ok the arms could go lower for flat and incline  but honestly it is a minor gripe that can be helped by simply replacing the bench with another or rising yourself higher on the bench somehow.  Yes, they could have fixed that part  but all the other thing make up for it! 

The bench is getting negative feedback  which is complete nonsense.  After using this machine and waiting on a small part that will allow me to finish the machine proper "which is on the way and was able to use something else temporarily" This bench is definitely worth keeping.

The criticism on the price.  Ok it is a little bit more expensive but you get a LOT not a little as Coop seems to think for that money. First off you get adjustable handle grips. "Who else offers that now?" and a much much more robust frame build that both looks far nicer and is much much stronger with a higher weight capacity. My only criticism about the bench is it could have little less rocking but when you are under load there really is none unless you try and shift your body weight on the bench. You can train unilaterally and get absolute full range of motion,  I know a set takes little longer but training unilaterally has many advantages too. So to me the criticism  about the bench is complete nonsense and way way overblown.  I personally love it!  

Lastly,  weight felt on this machine is heaver feeling "to me" then the weight truly is.  That is obviously due to the scissor leverage aspect of the machine and where the weight is on the lever.  There is some criticism about the arms being different length  and weight.  I can personally NOT feel this difference in weight. And before you go adding 5 extra lbs to the left arm that is lighter keep in mind that the weight from the handle is a little far back on the longer lever making up for that mechanical advantage for that slight couple lbs weight difference.  The set back equals out each arm to nearly exactly the same force to move them each equally.  It took me a lot of studying the anatomy of the machine to realize this and the leverage principle that implemented to accomplish this equality.  So do yourself a big favor and if you can buy this it is absolutely the best thing they invented so far in my opinion.

One thing he is not telling you about induction ranges are too full one unlike the commercial ones they have one regulator for all the burners, and if that regulator dies, your whole induction, cooktop is dead commercial versions have a regulator for each burner so that if one regulator dies, the rest of the stove can still be used but residential ones use the cheapest regulator they can find and that is the true point of failure and those regulators are not cheap. Secondly, they’re finding that a lot of the induction burners because they’re made with the cheapest parts you can find even though you’re using a induction safe pan it’s not recognizing the pan saying it’s too big or too small or something and it’s not working so my recommendation after looking at all the different induction stoves out there is weight 5 to 10 years before really getting an induction, the cost will come down and the reliability will improve

Also, with a gas stove, you have to have a certain distance between the stove and the vent fan plus you have to have a minimum 600 CFM fan to draw the gases away from you and not to fill the kitchen. If you get an over the range microwave with the fan built-in it will never be strong enough for a gas stove and most vent fans look great, but are not strong enough. Make sure you look at the manufacturers recommendations for a gas stove to ensure that you’re venting the gases out of your kitchen properly.

As for laundry machines sure speed queen is number one when you’re looking at reliability but if you look at a lot of the reviews nowadays, what’s happening is people are complaining that sure they may last 25 years but they also use a lot more water and people are finding that they don’t wash as well so they have to put a load through twice maybe three times to get it the same cleanliness as other manufacturers that you’re using more water more soap more energy so is it worth a machine lasting 2025 years if it’s not washing your laundry properly, so please keep that in mind when you’re spending money on a laundry machine speed queen will last forever but it may not clean your clothes properly and which is more important one that last 10 to 15 years but is reliably cleaning your clothes or one that lasts 25 years but you have to run it through twice

Also, in Canada speed queen is under the name of Huebsh. Still made by speed queen, but a different name and speed queen‘s new front load washer, which supposedly has a better cleaning quality and uses less water will not be sold in Canada. I contacted them and asked when that model will be available in Canada and was told with no uncertain terms that there is no plans for speed queen to sell the front load washer in Canada and my reply to them was that is a shame because there are a lot of people with mobility issues were a front load is far easier to use than a top load and it would be something that would actually be a feature people are looking for

Loved the video! 
What's really interesting is that over the past 20 years I have had two Whirlpool and one Samsung front load washers.
All three failed in the exact same way with the spider pulley beginning to disintegrate and then leaking from the bearings in the rear and the bellows in the front. 
I also had the unfortunate Samsung refrigerator with the notorious ice maker. 
The refrigerator was fine, The ice maker was not, they replaced it twice and it never worked correctly, ever. 
What's scary is that I have had an LG front load washer, one of their more reliable models, for 6 years and we have had an LG counter depth French door refrigerator for longer than that. 
Both appliances are performing perfectly. 
I think I got lucky with the refrigerator because I had read someplace or heard that the counter depth French door LG'S did not have the same model of compressor as the more problematic units even though it's still use a inverter compressor. 
Fingers crossed!
As far as the washer machine, after the three failures in the space of 12 to 13 years when I bought the LG I shifted gears heavily. 
Abandoned liquid detergent and fabric softener completely as they are known contributors to failure in washing machines. 
Now I use only powder detergent and I'm very careful about dosage not being too high, I also use vinegar for softener. 
Religiously use the cleaning cycle at least once a month or more if I do a lot of heavy laundry. 
Check the drain trap once a month to ensure nothing is getting clogged to damage the drain pump. 
I keep the door unlatched so I can get air and the detergent dispenser pulled out slightly so it can air out as well.
Overall the machine seems to be functioning and looks as good as it did when I bought it. 
I am hoping to get 10 to 15 years out of the unit before it needs replacement! 
Now for the big experiment.
Our electric dryer just recently began to go out so I did a lot of research. 
After watching some of your videos and videos on other appliance YouTubers channels I decided to pull the trigger on the new LG heat pump dryer that came out this year. 
As far as the dryer's functioning, I could not be happier it is an amazing machine. 
I feel I'm up to the task of being almost fanatical about maintenance on this machine. 
Always clean the lint trap, both of them, every time I do a load and I wipe the interior of the drum as well as run a condenser cleaning cycle about every 10 loads. 
So far I have been impressed with the lint system and condenser coil cleaning system. 
I've had the machine now for a couple of months and probably ran about 50 loads through it and there is no lint whatsoever on the coils which can be accessed through the front to the right of the machine.
I feel like I will do my very diligent best to keep the heat pump dryer for as long as I possibly can especially since it's very expensive compared to a standard electric dryer.
It's really is a superior machine and I don't mind the longer drying times because the advantages far outweigh that one negative. 
It's super energy efficient, gentler on clothes, and you don't have to have the vent to the outside to get clogged and need! 
I believe it is a way to the future!

Comment:
I love Jcrew. That said I usually shop their factory stores and thrift the higher end Jcrew. I always get compliments when I’m wearing their clothing. 

TJ Maxx is always hit or miss which is kinda their point. To me, style, convenience, price, & quality are the most important. & by quality, I mean how long will it last me - I don’t need something that will last generations because who wears stuff from their parents or grandparents anyway? No one I know. 

I’ve had TJ Maxx stuff pill after one wash. But the higher end & more expensive cotton Ralph Lauren polos always end up shrinking also so it’s wasted money either way. 

The shirts that hold up the best I’ve found so far are half and half cotton & polyester blends. No other materials. 60-40 cotton poly blend works well too.  I know polyester is considered a cheap material but yet it’s still found in high end clothing brands. I found a $300 polyester shirt at Saks Fifth Avenue for example.

I remember Kohl's from the early 2000s.  They sold good quality men's shoes.  Now 90% of the shoes they sell are garbage, like APT 9.  Shoe quality has degraded for many brands (thanks to private equity): Johnston & Murphey, Florsheim, etc.

I went to T.J. Maxx, Beal's, and Walmart for cotton or wool men's socks.  99% of what they had was 97% (or more) polyester.  I bought a pack of Dickie's that were 70% cotton.  The only cotton blend socks at Walmart were made by Gold Toe, everything else was polyester.  Also, I got a pair of wool socks from Walmart in the sporting section for hunters.  Tractor Supply had some cotton socks.  They even sold over the calf "boot" socks.

T.J.Maxx in the 1980s sold all cotton and wool socks for $3 to $4 a pair.  Now a days it is all over priced garbage.

We own both here is the breakdown:
1. Maintenance Ev wins.
EV have not done a thing to it besides rotate tires and have owned it about a year longer then PHEV. The PHEV is now needing the regular scheduled service. 

2.Smoothness/quiet EV wins.

3. 1 pedal EV wins barely but the Volvo PHEV actually is one of the very few that has real 1 pedal driving, 1 big reason we liked it. No other PHEV has as good of one as far as I am concerned. 1 pedal is awesome.

4. Long distance travel, PHEV wins. Our Honda EV gets close to 300 miles range. But the key here is the EPA range does not do a great job of comparison on long distance. Anyone driving a road trip generally takes the highway and generally is driving 70+. What you see on a sticker is mixed driving, EV are vastly superior in city under 50.

5. Winter range, both ice and ev experience range loss but ev are just more dramatic. So let’s say January in new England highway driving 4 hrs round trip no charging, you will have range anxiety.

6. Cost the ev wins, charge at home 95% time, next to zero maintenance, oftentimes PHEV jump to that from standard ICE are quite expensive. Deals can be had on the EV.

7. Performance, now this is a tough one, our Volvo is blazing fast, but typically EV will win.

8. Ease of use for most of what you do on a weekly basis, tie, however if you want to switch off your brain then the PHEV wins.

9. Remote adventures, PHEV wins. If you are driving somewhere in some remote parts of this country, the charging infrastructure can be super weak.

10. 2 car households, ideal scenario is 1 car is an EV, there is IMO no reason to have a 2 car household with 2 ICE vehicles. 1 should be an ev, better for the environment, and honestly just so buttery smooth, quick, cheap to maintain and easy to use daily it is a no brainer.

Final thoughts in a world where 400 mile range EVs are cropping up and flash charging of 5 minutes is already a thing in China and Europe, the future is EV. We would be a 2 EV household IF we had 1 of those things.

You might want to do your calculations again. As of July 2, 2026 the average price of regular gas in the US is $3.84. The average price of DC fast charging is between $0.47 and $0.53 per kWh. Let's take a Volvo XC60 and compare it to a Volvo EX60. You're supposed to use premium fuel in the XC60, but we're going to ignore that for this use case. The XC60 has an 18.8 gallon fuel tank. The EX60 P10 has a 91 kWh usable battery pack. If we look just at the straight cost to bring each from completely empty to completely full, the XC60 will cost you $72.19. The EX60 will cost you $48.23. Of course, I realize that's not a truly fair comparison. The XC60 will let you drive more miles. So, let's instead look at the cost per mile using Volvo's documented figures. The XC60 gets a combined fuel economy of 26mpg. Thus, at $3.84 per gallon, the cost per mile is $0.15. Now let's look at our EX60. It has a published range of 322 miles for the P10 variant. At $0.53 per kWh, that translates to $0.15 cost per mile. In other words, if you exclusively charge your EX60 using DC fast charging your cost per mile is the same as the cost per mile of the XC60 using regular fuel. Of course, if you are able to charge at home, the cost per mile goes down quite a bit. Average cost for residential electricity is $0.19/kWh, meaning the cost per mile drops to $0.05 if you do all of your charging at home.

I have to add a caveat to the information I shared above. It is based on published specs that may or may not reflect actual real-world values in your particular location. I used the Volvo 60-series because that line has ICE, PHEV and EV powertrains available. I did not account for any other factors such as efficiency loss when charging the EV battery or impact to EV range due to extreme weather conditions / driving habits.

A PHEV doesn't really have any good use case in the current environment. If the vast majority of your driving can be covered by the battery, get an EV. On the other hand, if the vast majority of your driving requires the ICE, then get the ICE, though a very compelling argument could be made to get the EV here as well. Comment:
As someone who owns a Kia Sportage PHEV here are some things I didn't realize until after buying it.

1. You have the best and worst of owning both systems. What do I mean? Your range for electric is great for daily not for long range but when it gets down to 20% its a normal hybrid which is now hauling a heavier battery. This sometimes takes away space from having a spare tire like for my vehicle. 

An engine is meant to run. It is not meant to be sitting for weeks. Even though you can live your life on all electric. DO NOT. Run it once a week to get fluids through it. It needs to run! Go on a 20-30min drive while in hybrid mode.

2. Your maintenance is now two systems. You may think, "I barely used my engine why do I need to change my oil every 5k?" An engine has the most wear and tear at start up. This happens all the time with a PHEV. At least with a hybrid it warms up, but not with a PHEV. Not unless you run it like a hybrid all the time which defeats the purpose. Change your oil every 5k. 

3. Normally your 12v battery is charged via your alternator. Well,  with an engine not running it comes down to an ICCU from the battery. Make sure you pay attention to your 12v. If your dash lights up like a Christmas tree, its most likely the 12v battery. Again hybrid mode using the engine will use that alternator. 

4. You'll have more added fluids and belts that need to be changed than just a normal ICE vehicle or only electric. And they gotta be done on time. 

5. When hard passing or getting on the highway with hard acceleration, the car will use the engine. Make sure to put your car in hybrid mode sometime before to get the engine warmed up. Or else you are requiring that engine cold to go to the max. That's a terrible idea. How would you like to wake up and have to sprint right away? Same principle. 

Do I regret buying my PHEV? No, not at all. But I bought mine used which took away the big hit of depreciation from it. Especially with it being the most costly of the Sportages. I've loved my vehicle and it suits my needs perfectly. Its so nice only filling up once a month. Those cost savings I feel go back into the added maintenance required but I also have the most powerful of the bunch so I see it as an equal. But I think for 90% of people a hybrid is the way to go.

The amount of range added per hour (or per minute when fast charging) is generally going to matter more than the amount of time to go from empty to full. The bZ wins on that front since it's more energy-efficient than the RAV4 (probably from being a bit smaller) and you could easily bank up a full charge over time even on 120V, although a level 2 charger adds a lot more flexibility. The RAV4 gets you about 2.7 mi/kWh, while the bZ officially gets from 3.2 to 3.8 mi/kWh depending on trim level.

The bZ and similar cars can now provide an experience pretty similar to a gas car where you drive several days and recharge around once a week with a level 2 charger or a public fast charger. 120V charging may or may not get you what you need, but it certainly extends the time between needing public charging, just like the PHEV reduces trips to the gas station.

The smaller battery and lower efficiency of the RAV4 means that you need to plug it in every day or two to make the best use of it. Perfectly fine if you have a home outlet, but if you don't, it's better to either stick with a regular hybrid or go full BEV.

Video_Title: England Survive Mexico! Post-Match Reaction
Comment:
I have to disagree with some of the tactical analysis here. 

Rice and Bellingham were switched over - Bellingham in the left-half-space and Rice in the right-half-space. This suits Bellinghams runs forward and Rice's crosses. We have seen this at times for England at the WC, but usually towards the end of games. They did this from the start. The first goal comes from Rice driving forward, something he is brilliant at but we hadn't seen until last night. Bellingham is going through the middle and arrives at the back post for his header.

The second goal comes from a smart press by Anderson and Gordon. These Anderson "jumps" have been problematic for the previous games but worked perfectly in that moment. 

The third goal comes from going long. Generally, I think the press wasn't amazing. At times Kane and Bellingham were keen to be aggressive and the rest of the team were more conservative. But, I think it would have been mad to try and come out playing PSG or Bayern Munich style aggression for the first 20-25 minutes. Tactically it was smart to be reserved. As I say, there was disconnection, which is concerning - but not greatly significant. 

Tactically, I doubt Spain, France or Argentina would have played it much differently before the first hydration break. Then the two quick goals probably shock England and Mexico. Then the Mexico goal comes from bad defending as the cross comes in and a good finish. Then I suspect England's thinking was '2:1 up at halftime in the Azteca sounds pretty good, let's not take any silly risks'. 

Overall, there were a few big moments which really really effected the game state. I don't think England were perfect but I think the tactics were spot on for the game, and I suspect very similar to what any other manager going for the WC trophy would have done. 

I love the tactical analysis at Tifo, and I'm not an expert like these guys. But I do really see it quite differently.

If you think the 345s and 710s are bad, come over here to Seoul (where people treat commuter and metro trains as the same thing)
and do the *full 4-hour journey* on Metro Line 1 with *no bins, no power sockets, no toilets,* and especially *_NO TRANSVERSE SEATING._*
It's gonna be a living hell for people like you.

That being said, I honestly don't understand why the brits love to bitch and whine about *literal commuter trains* like the 700s and 345s being "uncomfortable".
They're more than enough for the routes they serve, especially if you consider that you usually ride them for around an hour, or 2 hours at max.
If anything they should've had full longitudinal seating (+ folding seats) for extra standing room, _that's_ how you get extra capacity, it's a tried and tested method in countries like Japan and South Korea.
And we _definitely_ don't need those amenities, if anything I'd cut it at power sockets. Just use the loo and bins at the stations instead, it doesn't hurt you. If they don't exist, go build one.

Go ahead and curse me if you want, but I'm not changing my mind about Aventras being one of the best british trains.
British commuter trains (and generally any public transport vehicle with a maximum journey time of around 2 hours) _really_ need to stop being so "fancy", they're not hotel rooms, for fuck's sake.

i had one of the first dt602dces in the country and the firmware update was flawless but i will stress if you have one without the update its very worth doing as it fixed more than the annoying beep but it so simple to do.

I have a test that probably wouldn’t occur to you and that is the newby test, send someone into each shop who actually knows nothing about model railways but is eager to start in the hobby, the test breakdown should run as follows:
How long does it take before someone engages with them.

When engaged do they speak the same language or do they have a tendency to go into geek mode.

How realistic is the advice given.

Did the customer leave the shop with a purchase or just lots of advice/homework.

The reason for this type of engagement test is a hark back to an experience I once had at the then new PC World, way before they became part of the Curry’s empire, I walked around the place for about an hour being avoided by all the staff who should have had a sign up “PC World, by geeks, for geeks”, when I eventually cornered someone literally, the conversation was awfully one sided until this guy realised I had some knowledge of computers at which point he went through the sort of stuff that was in my budget to the top end, at that time the new 386 machines.

I basically grew up in model shops with my particular angle being aircraft both flying and static, but I had some 00 kit back in the day and dabbled with N gauge briefly, however I cannot stress enough that new folk coming into the hobby is vital to keep the hobby going and how new people are treated when they first pluck up the courage to walk into a model shop is vital for the longevity of the trade.

Comment:
The key is sell when it's high and buy when it's low, not the other way around. Think about it: if a stock is worth $400 when the Market is high, but drops to $200 when it's low, then buying at $400 and selling at $200 is a loss of $200. If you instead buy at $200, and later it goes up to $500, that's a profit of $300.

 People have it backwards. This is true even with gold. When it's price is high, commercials lie and say buy, but that's backwards. Don't get fooled. You should sell when it's high. If you don't have any gold or stock, what money you would use to buy it, you save. Then when it goes low, then use that to buy gold or stock.

Happy investing.

Edit: if it wasn't clear, when the Market drops buy more. Do not panic. Do not sell. It is an opportunity. If you couldn't afford $400 and it dropped 50%, you can now buy it for less. When it goes high, sell. Do not buy. If it goes up 25%, what you bought for less is now worth more. That's a profit. So when you buy as it drops to $200, then sell for when it rises to $500, that's 250% or 2.5× in profit. Go against the crowd.

When a store sells on clearance or discount, most people think "oooh free food." Most don't see the business is doing bad. They aren't selling that product, so they make deals to make more people buy them. It's high supply, low demand. So they discount it. When prices go up, it's a matter of high demand and low supply. So they sell at a higher price. Limited time offers, bundles, etc all follow these patterns.

Video_Title: Why Mutual Funds Over Index Funds?
Comment:
The data: 
1. The "Failure Rate" of Mutual Funds
Financial institutions track this performance via the SPIVA Scorecard (S&P Indices Versus Active). Their data shows that the longer you hold a mutual fund, the less likely it is to beat a simple index:  

1 Year: Roughly 65% of active managers underperform the S&P 500.  

10 Years: Roughly 85% of active managers underperform.  

20+ Years: Over 95% of active managers underperform.

The 30-Year Reality: Stochastically, the chance of an active manager beating the S&P 500 over a 30-year stretch is less than 1%.  

2. Why Index Funds Usually Win
The primary reason for the gap isn't that mutual fund managers are "bad" at picking stocks; it's the cost of doing business:

The Expense Ratio: * Index Fund: Costs roughly 0.03% to 0.10%.

Mutual Fund: Costs roughly 0.60% to 1.50%.

An active manager has to beat the market by at least 1% every single year just to break even with the index after fees.

Tax Efficiency: Index funds trade stocks much less frequently. This means fewer "capital gains distributions" that you have to pay taxes on compared to active funds.  

Human Error: Active managers often "churn" portfolios during market volatility, whereas index funds remain disciplined, capturing the full recovery of a bull market.

3. When do Mutual Funds actually win?
There are two specific "niches" where active mutual funds occasionally outperform the index:

Small-Cap Stocks: Because smaller companies are less researched by Wall Street, a skilled manager can sometimes find "hidden gems" that an index misses.

Fixed Income (Bonds): In complex bond markets with shifting interest rates, active managers tend to perform better than passive bond indexes.

Comment:
Sadly, this happens a lot.  I’m a nurse that used to work critical care. I took care of patients that actually had heart attacks and needed an angiogram with a stent, or open heart surgery. It always made sense on the inpatient side. 

Then I switched to outpatient interventional radiology. I’m no doctor, but I do know the literature. It’s becoming more and more apparent that they’re performing unnecessary angiograms and stent placements on patients. And it’s always on a spectrum. It’s not as if there are patients that are qualified, and patients that are not qualified. There are extreme cases where it makes absolutely no sense, And there are cases where it makes perfect sense. And then there’s a lot of gray in between. The financial incentives to do these procedures, make it far too easy for hospitals, outpatient clinics, and doctors to perform the procedure on patients that might benefit from more conservative approaches, like medication and lifestyle changes. Getting subjected to a poke to a major artery, contrast, damage to your body, bleeding, infection, kidney failure, side effects from the stent… I don’t think these risks are fully explained to the patient, nor do I think a lot of of them completely understand them. All they see is a cardiologist telling them that they need the procedure for their heart. They’re literally shoved in and out of these units with no support. Some of them died, some of them came back to the hospital with complications. I only lasted nine months doing it because the ethics of it all made me so sad.

It’s the financial incentives of our system that need to change. If these doctors are salaried, and there’s no financial benefit to doing more of these procedures, a lot of these malpractices will end.

Not sure if it’s been mentioned here, but labyrinthitis and vestibular neuritis are actually not the same thing though and so to differentiate, vestibular neuritis will NOT have hearing loss. If hearing loss is present, then it would be labyrinthitis. To differentiate labyrinthitis from Ménière’s disease, Ménière’s disease is a chronic relapsing course so there are recurrent episodes that can last for a few hours at a time and the symptoms can fluctuate as well, all progressing over time. Labyrinthitis is more of an acute consistent disorder that follows a viral prodrome and the symptoms are non-fluctuating and sustained.

Tl;dr: Vestibular neuritis will NOT have hearing loss, labyrinthitis will (profoundly). Labyrinthitis is not episodic or fluctuating, but Ménière’s disease is.

Updated USPSTF Guidelines (that were mentioned) as of August 2024:

1. Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Screening: One time abdominal ultrasound in men 65-75 years of age who have ever smoked.
2. Lung Cancer Screening: Annual low-dose CT chest in adults aged 50-80 with at least 20 pack year history of smoking and are currently smoking or quit within the last 15 years. Keep screening annually till they have quit for at least 15 years. 
3. Colon Cancer Screening: Q10year colonoscopy in adults aged 45 and older OR 10 years prior to diagnosis of 1st degree relative with colon cancer (whichever is earlier). Alternate screening options accepted by USPSTF - Q5year flexible sigmoidoscopy OR Q10year flexible sigmoidoscopy with Qannual FIT OR CT colonography Q5years OR Annual FIT or FOBT.
4. Cervical Cancer Screening: Q3year PAP smear (cytology only) in women aged 21-65. Q5year PAP + HPV co-testing in women aged 30-65.
5. Breast Cancer Screening: Q2year Mammogram in women aged 40 to 74.
6. Osteoporosis Screening: DEXA scan for all women aged 65 or above.

Diagnosis is confirmed on otoscopy by visualization of a bulging tympanic membrane (TM) and/or the presence of middle ear effusion (indicated by poor TM mobility on insufflation) with TM inflammation (eg, erythema).  Treatment with oral antibiotics is recommended in specific situations:

First-line therapy with amoxicillin is indicated for infants age <6 months and for children age ≥6 months with high fever (>39 C [102.2 F]), severe pain, or bilateral disease.  
Second-line therapy with amoxicillin-clavulanate is indicated for refractory symptoms after 2-3 days of antibiotic therapy or recurrent AOM (within 30 days) after antibiotic therapy.
Therefore, this patient with high fever and recurrent, bilateral AOM after recent antibiotics warrants a course of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate.

Ototopical antibiotic drops are used to treat otitis externa.  Presentation includes ear pain and discharge with edema and inflammation of the external auditory canal.

Otitis media with effusion (middle ear fluid without TM inflammation) can be observed for resolution.  Unilateral AOM accompanied by low-grade fever and mild pain can also be treated supportively and observed in patients age >6 months.  This patient has bilateral AOM with a high fever, warranting treatment.

Comment:
There has just gotta be a core issue with the way teams recruit in general. If every team can target and scholarship 35 guys and there are 138 teams in the game that means there are 4000+ scholarships ready to be offered in total. Each class of recruits is about ~2250 guys. There should be shortages and teams who miss out but absolutely not anyone who goes unsigned, especially 4 and 5 star guys at the rate its going.  I can only pretend like so many players chose to go play another sport in each class yk.

I agree, each and every 5 star needs to be an absolute dog fight, signing one should be a major win but a major price of hours and NIL all with no true guarantee they'll actually be as good as they're hyped up to be. 4 Stars need to be similar but some can slip through to mid-major or group of 6 programs because the big dogs are in fights for 5 stars and other 4 stars or you have great pitches. 3 Stars need to be more plentiful and have a much greater variance in overall. 3 stars NEED to be the bread and butter of most team's recruiting classes. Lower 3 stars will go to smaller programs with the occasional gem slipping to some MAC or sunbelt teams.  2 Stars I would argue could still be in the game because some gems in real life were two stars like Khalil Mack, Kirk Cousins, Justin Jefferson (for a bit of time), JJ Watt and many more were two stars and developed into amazing players. They should be rare gems though but still exist. 1 stars I probably agree they don't need to exist...they're bad even by the 138th ranked FBS team standard. Unless EA introduces multi-year recruiting or dynamic star ratings at the season progresses, I can't imagine the game needing any 1 stars and anywhere the amount of 2s we currently have. I wouldn't be opposed to lumping them together into one big "not ranked" section either tbh it would still allow for the occasional crazy gems and probably be easier for teams to be coded to not prioritize them. 

This all being said the devs are in a tough spot to balance realism and enjoyment in rebuilding teams. I think why we are seeing what we're seeing is they're making Dynasty too easy. Just before CFB27 came out I did a quick UTSA rebuild on 26, and I was able to in my first year grab up a five star, a few 4s and a bunch of really good 3 stars with minimal competition and then a stud transfer portal class. It is my belief that these 4 and 5 star players fall through the cracks to allow for us players to get these program shifting recruits and feel good about how "great" we are at recruiting. 

I think the best of both worlds would be adding a difficulty mode to dynasty itself. Lower difficulties would be experiences like what we see now, 4 and 5 stars are not being recruited, teams in big time conferences making nonsensical recruit classes, etc. While higher difficulty dynasty would simply be more akin to what you and I seem to want based on what I've written and what you said in your video.

Video_Title: Western Governors University (WGU) Review | Best Online Colleges for Busy Adults
Comment:
WGU has been a nightmare for me, and I am far from alone, just check their Better Business Bureau (BBB) reviews. Instead of professors, they assign "mentors" who routinely refused to unlock courses for you. Every course required back-and-forth emails over 10 days just to enable system functionality for taking tests. Of course this won't happen with your first few courses, but it will have when you start speeding through your courses as advertised. I've even had tests I passed flagged for audit and had to retake them with questions unrelated to the study materials.

WGU uses every tactic to slow students down, likely because it benefits them financially. Although labeled as a non-profit, their holding company is for-profit, exploiting tax benefits. The U.S. Department of Education’s Inspector General audited WGU and found they had improperly received over $700 million in federal aid by offering self-paced courses without adequate instruction or faculty interaction, violating federal requirements. Critics argue WGU prioritizes cost efficiency over educational quality, yet the Trump Administration dropped the investigation.

Students receive no meaningful assistance, requests for basic information, like exam source materials, are ignored. You will not be able to see if they are failing you on purpose because you are not allowed to see your tests, ever! 

They often withhold the indirect cost portion of student loans, requiring intervention from FAFSA. This is a common complaint reflected in BBB reviews. Transfer credits are another issue; even guaranteed credits from Study.com or Sophia.org are frequently rejected, forcing students to retake courses. Even when credits are accepted, their delays effectively cancel out any progress.

WGU manipulates online narratives too. Criticism on forums like Reddit often results in account bans, and they pay influencers, like YouTuber Mosh Jajador, to promote them. Many students never finish in six months or even a year; most of us spend 1.5 years or longer, often transferring to schools like TESU just to finish.

Save yourself the headache and research thoroughly before enrolling. WGU’s predatory practices do not live up to their promises.

Comment: I took the course and enjoyed it (a few glitches here and there but, overall, nothing too bad). I felt I had a great grasp of the material, accounting principles and felt confidant enough to take the test. So I prepared myself before the test, took it and failed. Here are my complaints: 1.) I feel the test is NOT reflective of what's in the course. I understand that they want the student to grasp "cause & effect" of various accounting transactions. As well as overall accounting concepts. However, they should have included more examples in the course material to prep the student better. My advice to ANYONE taking the test: don't bother remembering details in the course. Just try and grasp how the numbers on one side of the ledger will affect other ledgers and equations. And relate that, not in accounting terms, but more in sentences in laymen terms. Then and only then, will you potentially pass the exam. 2.). The final test is multiple choice on steroids. The chapter tests give you typical multiple choice (a, b, c and sometimes d), where you can see all possible answers side by side. Even with those, you have to choose the BEST answer. The final exam gives you ONLY one possible answer at a time. You can choose it or not. If not, it moves on to the 2nd possible answer, until you reach the last. If you get to one of the "next" answers and decide a preceding answer was better, you're out of luck! Again, the chapter test answers were all visible multiple choice. The final exam answers were not. Not representative nor preparing the student very well at all in my opinion. 3.) Because the final exam, I feel, was so different from the course, I truly had no way of knowing what answers I missed or got right in order to improve any lack of understanding. In a nutshell, I feel grateful I have a great understanding of Bookkeeping and its principles. I had no problems or issues with the end of chapter tests. I feel I'm ready to start to work making money at it! But spending a few months part time on the coursework ultimately did not get the badge I felt I deserved and am greatly disappointed. Kudos to you that did! Any light you can shed will be helpful & appreciated. -Thanks.

Comment:
It is not really the Plaza Hotel anymore. When Trump owned it, with his wife Ivanka running the day to day operations, they invested $millions to faithfully restore the hotel to its glory days. 

But after shady investors in the Middle East bought it, they immediately set about not to invest or preserve, but to monetize the hotel by cutting it up into overpriced condos, selling off the best rooms and suits, closing off the fabulous main entrance facing Central Park. 

Then they installed an escalator in the lobby, as if this was a department store, not a world class hotel. They created this new fake hotel lobby, on the side, where guests can still book a room but these are the worst rooms that nobody wanted, when the building was being chopped up into condos. Such a loss for New York! Today, the address means nothing. 

I would rate it a 3.6. Why so low? Because the truth is, this is not the Plaza Hotel! The main entrance to the real hotel is blocked off, the original grand lobby is blocked off. There is just a small batch of rooms on the back side of the hotel, facing a street and office towers. It’s a scam…

Meanwhile, in Taiwan, the government actively promoted a Chinese Cultural Renaissance to preserve what was being lost on the mainland, making traditional culture a core part of its education.

Educational Impact
Educated Chinoy (Filipino-Chinese) and Taiwanese individuals often learn about Chinese culture through formal education that includes classical literature, history, and philosophy like Confucianism, which emphasizes values like filial piety and social harmony. This provides them with a deep, nuanced understanding of their heritage. In contrast, many uneducated individuals in mainland China grew up in a period where traditional knowledge was suppressed, leading to a more superficial or fragmented understanding of customs, often lacking the historical and philosophical context.

Comment:
Well how about that? This movie was actually not bad, for me the Despicable Me franchise has been on a losing streak ever since the second movie, 3, 4 and both of the first 2 Minions movies were not good, and so I didn’t really expect anything out of this movie because I had already kinda given up on the franchise, but it was actually decent enough

With characters that’s usually not how the Minions movies roll, they’re more just an ensemble of random dudes doing the same stuff, but here this is the first time that I’ve ever really felt like they put more character into them, because the 2 that it mostly follows were guys that were lifelong friends, so like I said, I feel like there was a little more characterization in this one, and the premise is actually really funny, it’s like this very meta story about the minions wanting to make a movie and looking for real monsters to star in it, for the most part it isn’t just another “Minions look for bad guy to serve” movie, which also makes for some funny and actually kind of shocking jokes, not much of a spoiler but there’s a literal women’s rights joke in here, which shocked the hell out of me but also made me laugh, and biggest of all 1 of the minions who’s meant to be like the big douchebag is named Dick, and when you hear how they use his name it’s like “They definitely did that on purpose” and there’s quite a bit of voice talent in this movie, Jeff Bridges, Jessie Eisenberg, Trey Parker etc. Given its meta plot it seemed very fitting as well, and the slapstick is pretty much what you’ve come to expect from the minions, is it pure key jingling kind of slapstick? Yes, but at the same time there’s no real harm in it either

For me it’s flaws are for 1 while most of the plot is unique we also split the screentime with the rest of the minions who are still doing the whole looking for a master thing, which to me was a bummer because like I said, that plot is really getting old for these movies, I wish they would’ve just moved away from that plot entirely and just focused on the movie plot, the other is this really perplexing story about the minions wanting to serve this robot guy they encounter, at first when you see how he is and even where he lives I thought it was gonna build up to something that kind would’ve made up for me continuously asking “Why are we with this guy?” But it doesn’t go that way, it just leaves me, well, asking “Why are we with this guy?” And he just wasn’t that funny either, he didn’t irritate me or anything but I don’t think I laughed at a single thing he did either

But for a movie I had little to no interest in I walked out having a decent time, would I say the Despicable Me franchise is back? No, but this is a promising sign, the minions had more character than they’ve ever had before, the plot was really funny and led to some great meta jokes and while not amazing this was pretty enjoyable. 6/10

Comment: The movie was fine. It looked and sounded like a great movie. John Williams is amazing, Spielberg knows what he is doing, and the acting was excellent. There was even a news anchor who got emotional during her scene. It was a small part, but she did a superb job with it. HOWEVER ... in multiple instances, the characters in the movie were doing such colossally stupid things, that I could not longer suspend my disbelief. I would give some examples, but I don't want to put any spoilers out there. I will say this, I'm not talking about a person doing something under stress that they might not do if they had the time to think about it. The instances in the movie that I'm talking about were people doing something that no one would do if they had time to think about it. And something no one would really ever do if they were afraid and stressed and acting out of pure instinct. In the most egregious example, the character, while he was doing the ridiculous thing, kept saying to himself "Why am I doing this? Why am I doing this?" I'm sure in script writing school they tell you to make sure the viewers understand the character's motivation, however, having the character act like a complete and utter moron while repeatedly saying "why am I doing this" doesn't cut it. The sad thing is, if the writers had been just 5% more creative in a handful of scenes, the movie would have been amazing. In my showing though, the theater was full and by the halfway point, people were laughing and making comments. I suppose this is a small spoiler (very small), so stop reading if you don't want to know it, but during one very intense scene while 2 of the protagonists were about to get into a car in an attempt to escape the villain. They were surrounded by henchmen, any one of whom could have stopped them and the movie would have been over. And I was expecting the henchmen to jump in ... it really was tense. Well, it was at that moment that one of the two escapees decides it might be a good time to start asking the other escapee questions about what they were doing and where they were going. A guy behind me, who was stressed, not trying to be funny, called out "get in the damn car and discuss that after you get away." There were a lot more things like it that were hard to overlook.

Comment:
I agree with the part about beat detective (or any sort of post recording beat matching in general) but did anyone feel the explanation was a little misleading? For one, why play the metronome with one and not the other? Secondly I would say a computer “swing”, in the sense that certain rhythms, like those using triplets or dotted notes, have a sound that we recognize as swinging and they can be mapped out by a computer. Audiences can feel that swing even in completely electronic music and they dance to it. So I wouldn’t personally call the thing that’s lost swing. I don’t have a ton of experience recording but I once worked on something where the producer wanted to beat match the drums. To me it just lost the variation and looseness that the minute inaccuracy of a human musician imparts on music. But to be honest it was subtle. If I hadn’t been told I wouldn’t have known why the two sounded different. The drummer was very accurate (by regular human standards) the difference between the beat matched version and the original was tiny. 
Since then I hear it all the time especially when you compare metal from the 1980s and today. To me it almost sounds like a sort of tension in old recordings that have not been beat matched or modern live recordings that isn’t there in a lot of modern studio recordings. We can hear that they are playing it right but the notes flam just a little so we feel like it’s all about to fall apart. It’s more obvious in fast technical music where the artists are playing at the very edge of their ability (think old Sepultura) but you hear it in other stuff too. It might come up more often in a swinging rhythm in that the parts of a piece of music that make it swing, like dotted rhythms or triplets in something that is otherwise in 4/4, are kind of small. So when we hear real musicians swing, and hear those tiny inaccuracies that we don’t consciously recognize but just feel as a kind of vague looseness, it feel more exciting and alive than a beat matched swinging rhythm. I don’t think it’s swing itself that is lost though.

Sonny, I'm a big fan of your shows, especially the ones in Manila, where I now live. I have a suggestion.

If you haven't already, you should do a show on Humboldt County, Ca. some time. I lived there for 10 years and ate some of the best food of my life. Must visit sites:

1. Samoa Cookhouse (Samoa Island, the one in Humboldt County, not the South Pacific): lumberjack style meals with logging museum attached. No menu; everyone eats what's being served that meal, all you can eat. Not the best food in the world but a unique dining experience.

2. Larrupin Cafe in Trinidad (25 miles north of Eureka): More high-end and classy yet very casual (the waiters are allowed to have wine on the job, and do). Some of the finest food I've ever had. Must try the house specialty, Phyllo Chicken.

3. Speedy Taco Food Truck (Eureka): By far the best food truck food I've ever had. Incredible carne asada burritos and the tastiest salsa roja in the world.

4. Seascape Restaurant in Trinidad: Not the best food around but a great view of Trinidad Bay (last whaling port in America). Lots of history, and at Katy's Smokehouse up the street you can buy fresh Dungeness crabs right off the boats and locally smoked salmon from a fat surly guy... if he's still there.

Step-by-Step Instructions
Form the Ice Cream Dome

## 🍔 Classic Homemade Burger Recipe


### 🛒 Ingredients (Makes 4 burgers)

**For the patties:**

* 1 lb ground beef (80/20 for juicy burgers)
* 1 tsp salt
* 1/2 tsp black pepper
* 1/2 tsp garlic powder (optional)

**For assembling:**

* 4 burger buns
* 4 slices cheese (American, cheddar, or your favorite)
* Lettuce
* Tomato slices
* Onion slices
* Pickles
* Ketchup & mustard (or your favorite sauce)

---

### 👩‍🍳 Instructions

1. **Prepare the meat**

   * In a bowl, gently mix ground beef with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
   * Divide into 4 equal portions and shape into patties.
   * Press a small dent in the center of each patty (helps them cook evenly).

2. **Cook the burgers**

   * Heat grill or skillet to **medium-high heat (about 375–400°F).**
   * Cook patties 3–4 minutes per side.
   * Add cheese during the last minute so it melts.

3. **Toast the buns**

   * Place buns cut-side down on grill or pan for 1–2 minutes until lightly golden.

4. **Assemble your burger**

   * Bottom bun → patty → cheese → lettuce → tomato → onion → pickles → sauce → top bun.

---

### 🔥 Cooking Temperature Guide

* Medium-rare: 130–135°F
* Medium: 140–145°F
* Well-done: 160°F

Comment:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 8-9 medium sized vine ripe tomatoes
- 1. large or 2 small shallots, peeled and quartered
- 6 garlic cloves, peeled
- 1 + 1/2 tsp salt + additional to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp dried basil
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
- 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar
- 1 + 1/2 cups cottage cheese
- 1/2 cup chicken bone broth
- fresh chopped basil leaves, for garnish

Preheat oven to 400 degrees and grease or line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Add the olive oil, tomatoes, shallots, and garlic to the pan and sprinkle with the salt, black pepper, oregano, basil, and red pepper flakes. Use clean hands to evenly distribute the oil and spices.
Bake for 30-45 minutes, until the tomatoes are very soft. Let cool, then transfer everything from the sheet pan to a blender (if your blender is not big enough, you may need to do two batches).
Add the balsamic vinegar, cottage cheese, and bone broth on top and blend on high speed until completely smooth. Salt to taste.
Pour the soup into bowls and top with fresh basil leaves. Store in the refrigerator for up to four days or the freezer for up to a month.

Video_Title: Are Pre-Made Meal Boxes A Scam? I Tested 5 To Find Out
Comment: The amount of meat you get in these meals is miniscule. Here's how they scam you: All they list is grams of protein in the entire meal which includes the sides, sauce, etc. They don't give you the weight of the main and most important source of protein, the meat. 1 boneless chicken breast weighing 6 - 8 oz. has about 70 grams of protein. A 1/2 lb (8 oz) of 85% lean ground beef has 45 grams of protein. These entire meals have only 40 - 50 grams of protein which means the amount of chicken you get is 1/3 of 1 breast. The amount of beef is 3 - 4 oz. This may be fine for children or tiny women but certainly NOT average or above sized adults, especially MEN. I don't want a snack, I want a true, real, proper meal, not 1/3 of a meal. Don't fall for these meal delivery SCAMS.

I signed up for Forkful after seeing one of their ads. After entering my payment information, I was prompted to select meals. I only wanted 6 meals total, but their vegetarian selection was extremely limited and did not meet my expectations — so I decided to cancel immediately.

Within 5 minutes of placing the order, I went into my account to cancel. To my surprise, the first 6 meals were already marked as “processing” and I was told they could not be canceled.

I called customer service right away. The representative was dismissive and repeatedly stated that orders “cannot be canceled,” even though the order had just been placed minutes earlier. There was no attempt to resolve the issue, no flexibility, and no concern for customer satisfaction.

When a company locks you into an order within minutes and refuses to provide a cancellation window, that’s a policy consumers should be aware of.

I will be disputing the charge with AMEX and will not be using this service again.

If you’re looking for meal delivery with better vegetarian options and more reasonable customer service, I recommend CookUnity instead.

Proceed with caution.

Video_Title: A Budget Camera So Good, I Bought One Myself
Comment:
Hey there.  I had a similar experience.  I mostly shoot video for clients and hobby work, but I've gotten back into photography over the past couple of years.  I've bought a lot of gear trying to find the "right" option for me.  My experience has been mostly with Canon, Lumix, and Sony, and I'd never considered Nikon, thinking it was too "expensive" to try.  Well, I now have 4 Nikon cameras.  I have two Z50IIs, a Z30, and a Zfc. I bought all of them used and have been very pleased with the results.  The two Z50IIs have replaced my Panasonic G95s for my hobby YouTube production work.  They provide an out of the camera look that I'm pleased with and that saves me a lot of time in post.  I use the Z30 for a dedicated project which is all video content.  It don't like the overheating issues, but I've worked around them.  The Zfc is something I bought just for myself.  No reason other than I like the retro look and function.  I think Nikon really nailed that for me.  I also have an OM3 so I have something to compare it to and the Zfc goes with me all the time where my OM3 sits mostly in a bag.  The big, major really, advantage with the OM3 is IBIS.  If I know I'm going to be shooting telephoto handheld, I take the OM3.  I just also know that I'm going to have to spend time at the computer to get the images the way I want.  I've been unable to dial in the OM3's out of camera look to my liking.  That's on me though.  The camera can do it, it's just more complicated and detailed than the Nikon and I have not cracked that nut yet. 

Anyway, for anyone wondering about Nikon, give it a go.  I've been pleasantly surprised and very happy with my switch over.  

Thanks for the video.
Cheers
Rick

Comment:
I find these "recipes", in general, perfectly useless. There is no "one and only one" recipe for all of your pictures. Then  you say, ok I make a few then, that where the mess starts. Are you sure it wouldn't have been better with your n°3 than your n°8 ? ....It is because it all depends of your mood at the time, then what you remember having seen might in fact not be as good as what you can see on your screen, or reverse.
The all thing is essentially subjective and mood related. Try to take a raw image from ten years ago and apply your "finally best recipe" from today. Compare to your final result from ten year ago and the one you made today ! And seriously, ten days is already enough to have a different view, no need ten years. Your tastes change, your vision change. It is not because you make one picture with a Reala simulation that "it has to be reala for all pictures". We had no choice before during the film days.
So my two cents on this : use the standard colors/contrast/etc from your camera and concentrate on the picture itself, there is a lot more to gain here. If you are happy with what come out, then edit and adjust to your present mood. If one percent of your pictures are concerned, that's good. It means that 99% should be trashed away.
If you come back from a week end with thousand pictures (not souvenir ones), you probably should throw away 980 and have 20 keepers at best.....and that would be very good. Then it is a pleasure to edit 20 pictures, it is par of the fun and the pleasure of photography. Soooo......recipes, just another distraction from photography.

Make different routines for each season if there is a big climate shift. My summer routine is much shorter, with more intense exfoliation cause it is humid where I live. My winters are longer with more moisture involved cause it gets very dry. I’ve found having a summer and winter routine also is fun cause I get to change products a bit but also as I’ve aged what works in one climate doesn’t work in another. Good to keep in mind when you travel too. A little research can save yourself a lot of discomfort. Sunscreen sticks are horrible, use them on your body. If you have a lot of half used tubes of sunscreen like I have from trying stuff, take them on vacation. Great way to use then up is by wear them on your body. Korean sunscreen works better in water/sweat than I thought especially if you keep applying every 2hrs. Burned through my left over sunscreen on a vacation and left with barely any sun after 4 days laying on the beach. My culturally appropriated birkini helped with that too though.
